skill.name: golang-pro
skill.description: Master Go 1.21+ with modern patterns, advanced concurrency, performance optimization, and production-ready microservices.
skill.summary: Build modern Go services, CLIs, and microservices with concurrency, testing, profiling, and production deployment guidance.
skill.author: sickn33

content.value_statement: Go teams need reliable patterns for concurrency, APIs, performance, and deployment. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code toward production-ready Go solutions.
actual_capabilities: Guides Go 1.21+ language choices, module setup, and idiomatic project structure.
Designs concurrency patterns such as worker pools, pipelines, graceful shutdown, and backpressure.
Reviews API service architecture across REST, gRPC, middleware, authentication, and observability.
Plans testing strategies with table-driven tests, benchmarks, mocks, and integration tests.
Suggests profiling, memory tuning, database optimization, and production deployment practices.
limitations: It does not run Go tests, profilers, or deployment tools by itself.
It needs project context before making architecture or performance recommendations.
It is focused on Go and should not replace language-specific guidance for other stacks.
Security advice still requires environment-specific validation and review.

use_cases.title: Design a Go Service
use_cases.description: Plan a maintainable Go API with clean boundaries, middleware, storage, testing, and deployment concerns.

use_cases.title: Improve Concurrent Code
use_cases.description: Review goroutine, channel, context, and synchronization choices for safety, latency, and maintainability.

use_cases.title: Prepare for Production
use_cases.description: Add observability, health checks, configuration, security controls, and CI practices to a Go application.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Go Package
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of structure and idioms.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Go package for idiomatic structure, error handling, naming, and tests: [describe package and goals].

prompt_templates.title: Design a Concurrent Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Go concurrency approach for [workload]. Include cancellation, backpressure, worker sizing, errors, and test coverage.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Production API
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Go service design for [domain]. Cover REST or gRPC, middleware, storage, observability, security, deployment, and migration risks.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize a Go System
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this Go performance problem: [symptoms and metrics]. Propose profiling steps, likely bottlenecks, safe changes, and validation criteria.

output_examples.input: A team asks how to build a worker pool for high-volume jobs.
output: A recommended worker-pool structure with context cancellation and bounded queues.
A testing plan for shutdown, error propagation, and throughput.
Operational notes for metrics, queue depth, and retry behavior.

output_examples.input: A Go API has rising memory use and slow database calls.
output: A profiling sequence for heap, CPU, and database latency.
Likely causes such as retained buffers, unbounded caches, and missing query limits.
A validation plan using benchmarks, load tests, and production metrics.

output_examples.input: A service needs production readiness before launch.
output: A checklist for health checks, logging, tracing, configuration, and graceful shutdown.
Security review areas for secrets, input validation, authentication, and rate limiting.
Deployment guidance for containers, CI, rollback, and monitoring.

best_practices: Provide the Go version, runtime constraints, and current tooling before asking for architecture guidance.
Include existing package structure, test coverage, metrics, and performance symptoms when requesting reviews.
Ask for validation steps so every design or optimization has measurable success criteria.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for broad rewrites without sharing the service boundaries and operational goals.
Do not optimize Go code before collecting profiles, benchmarks, or production metrics.
Do not apply concurrency patterns without defining cancellation, backpressure, and error handling.

faq.question: What Go versions does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets Go 1.21 and newer, with attention to modern tooling and language patterns.

faq.question: Can it help with concurrency bugs?
faq.answer: Yes. It can review goroutines, channels, locks, contexts, race risks, and shutdown behavior.

faq.question: Does it generate complete services?
faq.answer: It can design and guide service implementation, but final code needs project-specific review and testing.

faq.question: Can it help with performance tuning?
faq.answer: Yes. It emphasizes pprof, benchmarks, traces, memory analysis, and measurement before optimization.

faq.question: Is it useful for DevOps work?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers containers, Kubernetes patterns, CI pipelines, observability, and production readiness.

faq.question: Does it replace security review?
faq.answer: No. It can suggest secure Go practices, but environment-specific security review remains necessary.
